findings.title: rawTokenId null check actually checks grantType again
findings.body: The second requireNonNull uses `grantType` as the object and the message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed". The rawTokenId parameter is never null-checked, so a null rawTokenId is accepted and stored. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`. Callers such as encodeTokenId would then produce ids ending in ':null' or fail later.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and the wrong substring index
findings.body: Two errors in one check. First, `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects exactly the token ids that carry the expected grant shortcut, so every CODE_TO_TOKEN, REFRESH_TOKEN, DEVICE and CIBA event assertion using this matcher fails for correct ids. It should be `!equals`. Second, the encoded prefix is `st(2)+tt(2)+gt(2)`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5, i.e. `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. The comment 'starts at character 4th char' is also wrong. As written, the matcher either fails for correct ids or passes for wrong ones, so these event tests cannot verify the feature.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes only because of an NPE from a null session factory
findings.body: The test catches RuntimeException and treats any exception as success. The provider is built with a null sessionFactory, and for grant shortcut 'ac' (absent from the map) getGrantTypeByShortcut calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(), which throws NullPointerException. The test therefore passes for an unrelated reason and does not check the intended 'unknown grant shortcut' IllegalArgumentException. It should assert the specific exception type and message, and use a stubbed factory.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on a public SPI interface with no default. Any third-party or downstream grant type factory that implements OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will fail to compile and, at runtime, the encoder will be unable to handle it. A default implementation or a documented migration path is needed.

findings.title: Unchecked cast of every OAuth2GrantType factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory
findings.body: postInit casts each factory returned by getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. Any OAuth2GrantType factory that does not implement that interface (possible for custom or older providers) causes a ClassCastException, which aborts server startup in postInit. The stream should be filtered with instanceof, or the failure should be made explicit with a clear message.

findings.title: Null shortcut from a grant factory causes NPE during map population
findings.body: If a grant factory returns null from getShortcut(), postInit inserts into a ConcurrentHashMap with a null key or value, which throws NullPointerException. The failure occurs during startup with no message naming the offending grant. A null check with a clear IllegalStateException would be safer.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
findings.body: The public `Context(Context context)` constructor was deleted from the public static Context class. Any code outside this diff that copies a grant context will no longer compile. The PR does not mention this removal, and it is unrelated to the encoding feature. If the removal is intentional it should be called out; otherwise the constructor should be restored (and grantType copied in it).

findings.title: Access token jti claim format changes for every issued access token
findings.body: initToken now sets the token id to the encoded form 'onrtac:<uuid>' instead of a plain UUID. The id is exposed as the JWT `jti` claim and in event details. Any client, resource server, or validation logic that assumes jti is a UUID, or that parses it as such, will break on upgrade. This wire-format change for all access tokens is not reflected in the PR description or in the tests that still check UUID-shaped token ids elsewhere. It should be explicitly versioned or documented.

findings.title: Javadoc says shortcut is 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2
findings.body: The getShortcut() javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider slices the encoded context into fixed 2-character parts and rejects anything else. A grant implementer following this doc would produce an unencodable shortcut. The doc should state the exact 2-character requirement.
